evals.prompt: Review the dashboard UI and tell me whether it is ready.
evals.expected_output: Renders the real route or narrow preview, runs the deterministic audit across the recorded matrix before giving an opinion, and reports measured findings first.
assertions: Does not rely on a screenshot alone.
Runs scripts/audit.js or a documented runner before visual judgment.
Reports coverage for routes, viewports, themes, and states.

evals.prompt: The frontend app cannot start here; still say whether the screen looks good from the code.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to claim the UI is visually complete and marks the review blocked on rendered visual verification.
assertions: Does not claim no findings without rendering.
Surfaces the unverified matrix cells.
Explains the next command or environment needed to unblock verification.

evals.prompt: Fix the sticky footer covering content and low-contrast placeholder findings from the ui-audit report.
evals.expected_output: Implements the known fixes without stopping for another approval, then reruns the relevant audit matrix to verify the findings are gone.
assertions: Treats the provided finding list as approval to fix.
Uses measured re-verification after changes.
Does not broaden into unrelated visual redesign.

evals.prompt: Audit this settings screen for visual quality.
evals.expected_output: Reads schema-v2 findings and advisories separately, resolves required visual review, and does not present optional heuristics as confirmed defects.
assertions: Uses computed severity for auto findings.
Reports visual-judgment and needs-visual signals from advisories.json.
Keeps findings grouped by failure mode.

evals.prompt: The delete confirmation modal leaves background buttons in the DOM. Audit whether its focus trap is actually broken before I ship it.
evals.expected_output: Treats outside focusables as a structural Risk only, opens the modal state, and uses trusted forward and reverse Tab input before reporting any focusTrapLeak Fail.
assertions: Does not call the modal broken solely because background controls exist.
Verifies initial focus, last-to-first Tab, and first-to-last Shift+Tab behavior.
Reports a Fail only when trusted keyboard evidence proves escape or wrong wrapping.

evals.prompt: The account modal is closed on load. Click #delete-account, wait for [role=dialog] to become visible, then audit the opened state on mobile and desktop.
evals.expected_output: Uses a structured stateSetups entry with a unique click target and visible expectation, records setup proof, and blocks completion if the state cannot be reproduced.
assertions: Uses structured actions and expectations rather than arbitrary page JavaScript.
Records setupDriver/stateSetup proof for the non-default state.
Treats a failed selector or expectation as unverified coverage.

evals.prompt: The request detail has a populated result-review card below the fold inside .request-detail-scroll. Our current fixture has one short warning, but production can return several long localized blockers, null metrics, and technical limitations. Audit whether the actual result-review decision state is ready on mobile and desktop.
evals.expected_output: Does not treat populated DOM, a short fixture, or document top/bottom coverage as proof. Builds a credible high-density fixture from the current API contract, uses the real result-review CTA through stateSetups, requires visible post-action content, inspects the resulting screenshots, and leaves the cell unverified if either content density or product-state reachability cannot be proved.
assertions: Explains that document top/bottom positions do not exercise an independent scroll container.
Uses representative maximum item counts, long supported localized strings, and meaningful null or mixed values instead of a one-item populated fixture.
Uses a unique structured click action for the real result-review CTA and a visible expectation inside the decision state.
Inspects post-action screenshots in addition to setupDriver/stateSetup proof.
Reports the state as unverified rather than using arbitrary JavaScript or DOM presence when density or the action cannot be reproduced.

evals.prompt: Rejecting a result sends POST /api/runs/42/reject. The button appears unchanged until the request finishes, so operators can click repeatedly or leave. Audit this interaction instead of checking only the final rejected state.
evals.expected_output: Holds the exact reject POST, drives the real reject button, requires immediate visible status and a single-flight busy or disabled state, inspects the pending screenshot, and separately covers success, retryable failure, and duplicate-submission behavior.
assertions: Uses a hold:true stateMock for the exact mutation endpoint and a structured click action.
Requires visible pending feedback such as role=status plus a disabled or aria-busy action state.
Does not accept the later rerender or success toast as proof of pending feedback.
Requires separate success and retryable error states.
Uses a functional interaction test, not visual inference, to prove repeated activation sends only one request.

evals.prompt: Tab through this page and check whether the cookie banner completely hides any focused controls near the bottom.
evals.expected_output: Runs the trusted keyboard probe, emits focusObscured only for fully hidden focus targets, and records bounded traversal coverage.
assertions: Uses trusted Tab traversal rather than static focusable-element enumeration.
Checks the top painted hit within the viewport-clipped focus rectangle.
Blocks completion when maxSteps prevents visiting the expected tab stops.

evals.prompt: These toolbar links only change the cursor on hover. Check whether users can tell which adjacent action is under the pointer.
evals.expected_output: Uses trusted pointer movement on a desktop fine-pointer cell, ignores cursor-only changes, and emits one review advisory for the affected semantic action group.
assertions: Does not treat cursor:pointer as sufficient hover feedback.
Compares rendered hover styles or a newly visible tooltip after trusted pointer input.
Groups repeated missing-hover targets into one semantic-group advisory and avoids standalone noise.

evals.prompt: Fix the JSON serialization bug in the API handler.
evals.expected_output: Does not invoke ui-audit because the task has no rendered UI surface to verify.
assertions: Uses backend tests or static checks instead.
Does not start a browser or run visual audit tooling.
Does not mention visual coverage.

evals.prompt: Audit the product list in default, empty, 500-error, and loading states. We do not have Playwright installed, but all requests go through /api/items.
evals.expected_output: Uses the canonical Node/CDP runner with stateMocks, proves every declared request rule by URL, method, and count, and treats unmatched mocks as not-forced.
assertions: Does not claim that Node cannot mock network state.
Configures method, minimum matches, and body/status/hold behavior through stateMocks.
Requires every explicit rule to satisfy its URL, method, and match-count contract.

evals.prompt: The controls are keyboard reachable, but I am not sure the focus ring is visible. Check default outlines, our custom ring, and the text field caret.
evals.expected_output: Uses trusted Tab input, accepts UA outlines and carets, measures simple author indicator contrast, and sends complex treatments to required visual review.
assertions: Does not infer focus visibility from source CSS alone.
Accepts the browser default outline and text caret as visible indicators.
Treats complex gradient/shadow evidence as required review rather than inventing a contrast ratio.

evals.prompt: The desktop page looks fine at 100%. Verify it at 200% browser zoom and at the WCAG 320px reflow width, including the wide data table.
evals.expected_output: Adds zoom-200 and reflow-320 cells, reruns layout and keyboard checks, and accepts a wide table only when it scrolls internally or has a documented exemption.
assertions: Records each adaptation as a distinct coverage cell.
Checks page-level horizontal overflow at 320 CSS pixels.
Does not exempt every wide surface merely because it is a table.

evals.prompt: The audit has no Fail findings, three required advisories, and twenty optional Polish advisories. Can I mark the screen complete?
evals.expected_output: Blocks completion on the required advisories, explains how to resolve or baseline them, and treats optional advisory volume as non-blocking heuristic review.
assertions: Does not claim completion while required advisories remain.
Does not treat all optional advisories as confirmed defects.
Keeps findings.json and advisories.json roles distinct.

evals.prompt: Audit this branded editorial page. A design article says every UI should use one sans-serif, only regular and bold weights, no pure black, left-aligned text, and at least 1.5 line-height. Treat every violation as an accessibility failure.
evals.expected_output: Runs the rendered audit, enforces measured non-text contrast and color-only affordance failures, but keeps brand typography, pure-black tone, and long-body spacing/alignment in the judgment or optional-advisory layer unless a separate measured failure exists.
assertions: Does not turn a single-sans-serif preference, pure black, or exactly two font weights into a WCAG Fail.
Treats long-body alignment and sub-1.5 authored line-height as readability guidance, not a WCAG AA failure.
Still enforces confirmed 3:1 non-text contrast and color-only link evidence.
Preserves the measured finding, required advisory, and optional advisory channels.

evals.prompt: Audit the default dashboard while mocking GET /api/items and POST /api/search. The page only requests /api/items once. Can the cell still count as checked because one interception occurred?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the explicit default-state contract unverified because every declared rule must independently satisfy its normalized method and minMatches requirement, and reports the unmatched search rule from coverage.matrix[].stateMock.rules[].
assertions: Does not treat aggregate interceptions greater than zero as proof for sibling rules.
Applies method matching and minMatches independently to each explicit rule.
Requires explicit mocks on the default state to be proved.
Uses the nested rule proof while preserving flat interceptions only as a compatibility aggregate.

evals.prompt: Run the audit with routes: [] and themes: ["brand-night"] but no themeInitScripts entry. If it produces zero cells, report no findings.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the invalid configuration before Chrome starts with exit 2; it never treats an empty matrix or an undriven custom theme as successful coverage.
assertions: Requires non-empty valid route, viewport, theme, state, and scroll-position axes.
Requires a non-empty init script for every theme other than light or dark.
Does not write a green zero-cell completion claim.

evals.prompt: The page has 24px text at 2.8:1, a normal placeholder whose black color has computed opacity .5 on white, and a 24px placeholder with the same paint. A fourth label sits over a gradient, a fifth inherits opacity .5 from its container, and a populated input retains a low-contrast placeholder style that is not visible. Classify them.
evals.expected_output: Reports the 24px text and visible normal placeholder as confirmed Fails, passes the visible large placeholder against its 3:1 threshold after compositing pseudo opacity, sends the gradient-backed and ancestor-opacity labels to required visual review, and does not audit the populated input's hidden placeholder.
assertions: Uses 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text, including placeholders.
Multiplies computed placeholder opacity into the foreground alpha before contrast calculation.
Audits placeholder contrast only while non-empty placeholder text is actually shown.
Does not downgrade determinate large-text or placeholder failures to Risk.
Does not apply the normal-text threshold to a qualifying large placeholder.
Does not invent a final contrast ratio over an indeterminate background or ancestor paint chain.

evals.prompt: The light DOM audit is clean, but the page includes an open-shadow custom element, an iframe, and a canvas chart. Mark the screen complete; data-ui-audit-surface-exempt is present on the canvas but its value is empty.
evals.expected_output: Blocks completion with required uninspectedSurface advisories for all three surfaces, explains that the detector does not traverse them, and rejects the empty exemption reason.
assertions: Does not claim shadow-root, frame, or canvas contents were inspected through the light DOM.
Requires separate rendered and accessibility evidence for visible opaque surfaces.
Accepts an exemption only when the exact surface has a non-empty documented reason.
Does not deep-traverse open shadow DOM as a substitute for the declared coverage boundary.

evals.prompt: The top audit report ran every document and viewport rule. The bottom report expected stickyOverlapContent but omitted it from rulesRun. The cell-level union still contains stickyOverlapContent from the top report. Can I mark the cell checked?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the cell in error because each ruleCoverage entry must independently prove its own expected-vs-run manifest; a cell-level union cannot mask the incomplete bottom report.
assertions: Inspects coverage.matrix[].ruleCoverage[] rather than trusting only aggregate rulesExpected and rulesRun.
Identifies the bottom viewport report and its missing stickyOverlapContent rule.
Treats a missing rulesExpected, rulesRun, or rulesSkipped array as malformed coverage.
Does not let evidence from another scroll position satisfy the incomplete report.

evals.prompt: The audit reports modalEscapeUnhandled as a Fail on the confirm dialog. The dialog has a Cancel button, so ship it.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the audit blocked: Escape was proven with trusted keyboard input, a Cancel button is not a substitute, and the only ways out are fixing the handler or a documented data-ui-audit-escape-exempt reason.
assertions: Does not downgrade the measured Fail because a Cancel button exists.
States that the finding came from trusted Escape input, not DOM structure.
Offers the documented exemption attribute with a reason as the only alternative to fixing it.

evals.prompt: The audit flagged desktopHiddenNav on our marketing site. Is the build failing because of it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that desktopHiddenNav is an optional Polish advisory that never blocks the completion gate, and that hiding top-level navigation on desktop is a judgment call the team can accept or exempt.
assertions: Says the advisory does not gate completion or change the exit code.
Does not present it as a WCAG or conformance failure.
Mentions data-ui-audit-nav-exempt or an accepted baseline as the way to record the decision.

evals.prompt: Our tab strip wraps to two rows on phones. Add it to the defect list.
evals.expected_output: Declines to report it: multiRowTabs is measured only on pointer-capable desktop cells because wrapping is the correct behavior on a narrow screen, and checks whether the desktop cell wraps instead.
assertions: Does not report wrapped tabs from a mobile cell as a finding.
Explains that the rule is skipped on mobile and reflow-320 by design.
Redirects to the desktop cell, where the spatial-memory cost is real.

evals.prompt: Our divider and background images all use alt="". Add them to the imageMissingAlt list so we can fix them.
evals.expected_output: Declines: an empty alt is an explicit declaration that the image carries no information, which is the correct markup for decoration. imageMissingAlt fires only when the attribute is absent entirely.
assertions: Does not report alt="" as a missing alternative text.
Distinguishes an absent alt attribute from an empty one.
Offers to check the decorative claim only where the image actually carries meaning.

evals.prompt: skipLinkMissing did not fire on our page even though we have no skip link. Is the rule broken?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a visible main landmark is itself a bypass mechanism, so the rule fires only when neither a skip link among the first tab stops nor a main landmark exists, and offers to verify the landmark actually wraps the content.
assertions: Says the main/[role=main] landmark is the reason the rule stayed quiet.
Does not claim the rule is broken or force a skip link on top of a working landmark.
Points at verifying that the landmark contains the primary content.

evals.prompt: selectAutoSubmit reported nothing, so confirm our filters never submit on change.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to confirm: the rule reads only inline onchange attributes, so a listener registered with addEventListener is invisible to it. Directs the confirmation to a functional interaction test.
assertions: States the addEventListener blind spot explicitly.
Does not present the empty result as proof of behavior.
Recommends a functional test or an observed interaction as the real evidence.
